A severe storm system that brought high winds and heavy rain as it moved along the East Coast on Thanksgiving Day has left hundreds of thousands of utility customers without electricity, with restoration efforts continuing into Friday.

The combination of high winds and saturated ground toppled trees and power lines across the mid-Atlantic, contributing to the widespread outages. Utilities warned that rain-soaked soil increased the risk of additional failures overnight.
